independent_model_contract:
# Conditional full-eight early-high model review

This is a review of a necessary-condition encoding, not a new GF16 circuit,
an unrestricted lower bound, or an independent proof of the published
two-output theorem. No solver was run by this audit.

## Exact quotient represented by the residual variables

Work with zero-preserving Boolean functions on eight raw bits. Let H(f) be
the ANF part of degree at least three. Let I2(f) be the unique zero-constant
degree-at-most-two function agreeing with f on singleton and pair inputs.
The 219 coordinates of R(f)=f+I2(f) on inputs of weight at least three form a
linear map with kernel the 36-dimensional zero-preserving quadratic space.
Hence linear dependencies among residual vectors are exactly dependencies
among H(f), even though their coordinate representations differ.

At a support S of size at least three, the encoded residual is

    f(S) + (|S| mod 2) sum_{i in S} f({i})
         + sum_{{i,j} subset S} f({i,j}).

The support restriction on both sums is essential. The formula assumes
f(0)=0. The encoder uses only zero-constant linear operands, so every gate
has value zero at input zero and constraining the other 255 rows is exact.

Write r_i=rank(H(g1),...,H(gi)). The first gate is quadratic, so H(g1)=0.
Conditional on r8=r5, precisely the following equations are needed:

    R(gj) = sum_{i=2..5} c[j,i] R(gi), for j=6,7,8.

There are four unrestricted GLOBAL selector bits per late gate and 219
coordinate equations per gate. Early residuals need not be independent;
coefficients need not be unique. No full-rank, pivot, rank-two, or
last-quadratic restriction is justified. Equality of full gate truths would
be too strong: the difference is allowed to be an arbitrary quadratic.
The first-five nonzero condition is one OR over all 4*219 residual bits.

The executed finite controls check all 32,768 width-three four-vector/target
membership cases, including dependent representations, and identify the
residual map's rank 219 and kernel dimension 36. These are encoding controls,
not substitutes for the theorem dependency below.

## Why r8=r5 is conditional on the two-output theorem

Let E_i be the first i selector coordinates, and let H be the high-part map
on eight gate selectors. Choose a four-dimensional decoder section D
mapping injectively onto the target space modulo raw affine functions.
Since all four targets are quadratic, D is in ker H. Set
K_i=ker(H restricted to E_i) and s_i=dim(D intersect E_i). Then

    8-r8 >= dim(D+K_i) = 4+i-r_i-s_i,
    r8-r_i <= 4-i+s_i.

The published unrestricted two-quadratic-output theorem, together with the
measured pair lower bound, implies s5<=1: otherwise a five-gate prefix
computes two independent field components. At i=5 the inequality gives
r8-r5<=0; monotonicity gives equality. This argument does not require gate
truths to be independent. The separately reviewed quadratic-flattening
lemma and certified raw-parallel eight-gate exclusion imply r8>0, hence
r5>0. A raw-parallel pair lower bound alone does NOT establish s5<=1 for
nonquadratic prefixes.

Dependency: runs/aes-norm-pair-theory-20261018/proof.md records the
Mirwald--Schnorr theorem attribution via Boyar--Find and Bilgin. This audit
has not inspected the original theorem's full proof and does not replace
that explicit literature-dependency boundary with a local proof claim.

## Nested target flags and free affine corrections

If four target classes are available after eight gates, a prefix of i gates
contains at least i-4 independent target classes: the suffix can add at most
8-i dimensions. Choose nested Q by gate five, a second independent target
R by six, and a third independent S by seven. The measured semilinear action
on the JOINT flag (Q,span(Q,R)) permits Q=1 and R in {2,4,12}. R and R+Q are
interchangeable using the already available Q decoder. The third covector
must remain free outside {0,1,R,R+1}; all twelve remaining values are legal.
The production four forbidden assignments implement exactly this test.
All four original target outputs and all three prefix witnesses retain
unrestricted coefficients on the raw eight input signals.

For a determinant-one field matrix, inputs transform by

    a'=alpha*a+beta*b, b'=gamma*a+delta*b,
    a'b'=ab + alpha*gamma*a^2 + beta*delta*b^2.

Field squaring is binary-linear, so SL2 fixes all four field-output polars
pointwise and changes each exact output only by a raw-linear correction.
It is transitive on nonzero raw covectors and therefore permits fixing the
first useful left factor to mask one without fixing its right factor or
its plane. Raw-linear decoder terms must remain available to absorb those
corrections. This normalization can be applied after the joint flag
reduction because every target covector is fixed modulo raw-linear terms.

Input substitution preserves the degree-at-most-two space. Residual span
relations are therefore invariant, but the 219 coordinate vectors do not
literally remain unchanged or commute with substitution. Their quotient
classes transform invertibly.

## Gate-plane canonicalization and constants

Changing a Boolean operand-plane basis can add an operand to its product:
u(u+v)=uv+u. A dependent gate's operand may contain earlier NONLINEAR gate
truths, so this correction is not in general raw affine. Completeness uses
triangular rewrites of every downstream operand and every decoder in the
entire earlier-signal span. Then each transformed g_j equals g_j plus an
available earlier-signal combination, preserving every prefix span and its
high-part image. The late-span equations remain satisfiable with possibly
different coefficients. It would be unsound to permit only raw-affine
corrections at dependent gates or to freeze the late selectors in advance.

Affine operand constants can likewise be removed by triangular rewriting:
(A+c)(B+d)=AB+cB+dA+cd. Redundant/affine gates can be removed and zero gates
padded at the end; a nonaffine computation has a first useful gate with
nonzero raw operand plane. The source permits zero-left padding. No
intergate ordering, fixed first right factor, or fixed first plane is added.

## Executed source/model audit

An independent emitter reconstructs all five plain CNFs byte-identically,
including signed-native-XOR chain translation. The only imported code is
our immutable independent algebra helper, not production code.

The positive generic control replays all 380,106 clauses, 8,055 native XORs,
31,698 AND helpers, 2,040 gate truth variables, 1,533 residual variables,
12 late selectors, and 657 residual-coordinate equalities. Independent
scalar and bit-sliced replay agrees for all 256 inputs, all four outputs,
and all three prefix witnesses. Its final gate is cubic and r5=r8=3, so
this is an actual positive control for a nonquadratic last gate.

The fixed negative still computes all four generic targets but has r5=3
and r8=4, with the new direction introduced only at the last gate. Its
span contradiction is verified algebraically, independently of the
solver's uncertified UNSAT answer. All three main field probes are UNKNOWN
and exclude nothing. No complete GF16/AES candidate results from this run.

Karpathy guidelines influenced this review by keeping the change isolated,
making the conditional scope explicit, and checking both admitted and
rejected controls rather than treating an intended encoding as evidence.
